ing: thinned with a splash of milk
st: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Rub in the shortening with your fingers.
Stir in about [[1 cup]] warm water and knead for 5 minutes to a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a thin round about 8 inches wide.
Cook each tortilla in a hot dry skillet over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side until blistered in spots and soft. Stack in a towel to keep warm.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble them in a pan with [[1 tbsp]] oil until just set.
Spread warm beans over half of each tortilla.
Add a spoonful of crema, cheese, a little egg and avocado slices.
Fold the tortilla in half and eat right away.
Rub the steak with the lime juice, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Rinse the rice and cook it with [[3 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot over low heat.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a cast-iron pan over high heat. Cook the steak for 4 minutes per side for medium, until it reaches 145°F (63°C). Rest 5 minutes and slice across the grain.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the plantain slices 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and caramelized. Drain.
Plate the rice, beans and sliced steak.
Add the plantains, cheese, crema and avocado alongside, with lime wedges.

ing: cleaned, thinly sliced or diced (or use clams)
st: Put the conch in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered for 30 minutes until it begins to soften.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a second pot. Cook the onion, bell pepper and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the achiote and stir 30 seconds. Pour in the conch with its broth and the coconut milk.
Add the cassava, plantains, green banana and whole chili. Simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Cook until the cassava is tender and the conch is soft, adding water if too thick.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] salt, the lime juice and half the cilantro.
Remove the chili. Serve hot, topped with the remaining cilantro.

ing: whole red snapper or other firm white fish
st: Rub the fish with the lime juice and [[1 tsp]] salt. Let it rest in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Put the coconut milk, [[2 cups]] water, onion, bell pepper, garlic, tomato and chili in a large pot. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the cassava and plantains. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Gently lay in the fish steaks and spoon a little broth over them. Do not stir.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes. Add the shrimp if using and cook 3 minutes more, until the fish flakes and the shrimp are pink.
Add [[1 tsp]] salt to taste and half the cilantro.
Remove the chili. Serve in deep bowls with the rest of the cilantro on top.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt, the garlic powder and pepper. Let it rest 15 minutes, then coat with the flour.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the chicken in batches for 15 to 18 minutes, turning, until deep golden and it reaches 165°F (74°C). Drain on a rack.
Raise the oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the plantain slices in batches 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Toss the cabbage, onion and lime juice with a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.
Pile the plantain chips on plates and top with the chicken.
Add the slaw, then drizzle with ketchup and mayonnaise (and hot sauce if you like).
Put the cassava in a pot, cover with water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and boil for 25 minutes until tender. Drain.
Make the slaw: toss the cabbage, tomatoes, onion, juice of 2 limes, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Set aside to marinate.
Put the pork in a wide pan with [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cook uncovered, stirring now and then, for 40 minutes, until the water evaporates and the pork starts to fry in its own fat.
Keep cooking another 15 minutes, turning, until the pork is deep golden and crisp, and it reaches 145°F (63°C).
Drain the pork on paper towels and chop into bite-size pieces.
Arrange the cassava on a plate with the pork and slaw on top. Serve with lime wedges and hot sauce.
Boil the diced potato in salted water for 8 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the beef and garlic and brown it for 8 minutes, until it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper, potato and rice. Cook 3 minutes and let cool.
Mix the masa harina with [[1 tsp]] salt, then add about [[1.5 cups]] warm water to make a soft dough that does not crack. Rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 balls. Press each between two sheets of plastic to a 4-inch circle.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle, fold over and press the edges to seal. Crimp with a fork.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the turnovers in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with pickled cabbage or hot sauce.
Cut each tortilla into 6 wedges.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until a wedge sizzles at once.
Fry the wedges in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Warm the beans in a small pot or the microwave until loose and spreadable.
Arrange the chips on a plate and spoon the beans on top.
Scatter the cheese over the beans, then add the pickled onion and a drizzle of crema if using. Serve right away.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x13 inch pan.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Beat the egg yolks with [[0.75 cup]] sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Mix in the whole milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla, then fold in the flour mixture.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy, then add [[0.25 cup]] sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the batter in two additions, gently so the batter stays airy.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 20 minutes.
Whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk and [[1 cup]] cream. Poke holes all over the cake with a fork and pour the milk mixture over it slowly.
Chill for at least 3 hours so the cake soaks up the milk.
Whip [[1.5 cups]] cold cream with [[1 tsp]] vanilla to soft peaks and spread over the cake. Dust with cinnamon and serve cold.
